target_name: Erratic equity funding versus revenue growth
rationale: This is a mechanical leg-swap between two already-archived signals (VOL-of-share-growth vs. turnover trend, and share growth vs. revenue growth) rather than a new mechanism, so it is closer to a cosmetic recombination than a substantively different test.

This is the archive's dvc/(dvc+prstkc) − che/lct signal with two minor substitutions (dvt for dvc, che+oancf for che) and an unchanged hypothesis, i.e. a cosmetic variant of an already-evaluated signal rather than a new economic test.

The expression is the archive's best-alpha signal re-aggregated with MIN instead of a wedge — a pure functional-form tweak whose likely outcome (alpha collapse under conjunctive truncation) was already demonstrated by the generation-0 MIN composite in this same archive.

The "runway" construct is genuinely new, but using ABS(oancf) in the denominator conflates large cash burners with strongly cash-generating firms in the same low-ratio bucket, so the liquidity leg does not measure the deadline the hypothesis describes and its natural direction is ambiguous.

target_name: Multi-year payout drain against an eroding earnings base
rationale: The stock-depletion framing and the retained-earnings trajectory leg are a legitimately different angle from the archive's liquidity-flow payout tests, though the RE-trend leg risks being largely a slow-moving profitability proxy (and thus FF5/RMW-spanned) while the high-payout leg pulls in the opposite return direction, so the two legs may partly cancel.

This is the archived retirement-share signal with the liquidity denominator swapped and the expected sign reversed to match a single mixed archive result (FMB +2.0 but LS alpha −1.7% with t −1.4), so the "direct evidence" claim is overstated and the proposal amounts to sign-fitting a near-duplicate expression.
